analysis.title: India as an anti-AI trade
key_insights: INDA and SOX have moved in an almost perfect inverse relationship during the latest AI selloff. The Market Ear first outlined the India vs AI hype relative trade in mid-October and says it has played out well. Given the size of the outperformance, it would not get too greedy at these levels.

JPM data show India's rolling 12-month performance relative to emerging markets recently hit its weakest level in two decades, a lag of roughly 60 percentage points. The recovery has only just begun and the dislocation remains extreme.

EM funds are running significant underweights in India relative to benchmark, a reversal from the large overweights of the mid-2010s. A return to benchmark-neutral positioning by foreign long-only funds could bring in about $115 billion, per JPM.

MSCI India trades at 18.5x forward earnings, a 13.4% discount to its 10-year average of 21.4x. Banks trade at a 19% discount and real estate is almost 40% below its historical average. Small caps still trade at a 31% premium to their long-term average, so the valuation opportunity is uneven.

71% of MSCI India companies have beaten expectations this reporting season and 16% have missed, the strongest beat/miss ratio in more than two years. With about two-thirds of companies reported, Q2 FY27 earnings growth is tracking above 20% YoY, double the pace of two quarters ago. Earnings revisions are turning higher.

Private-sector project announcements in India rose from roughly 10% of GDP in FY23 to around 16% in FY26, per JPM. Investment is picking up in power, renewables, semiconductors, EVs, metals and real estate. Peak electricity demand is projected to rise from 271GW to 459GW by 2035-2036.

India imports 85-90% of its crude, so falling oil prices help inflation, the rupee and corporate margins. In the previous oil-relief rally, real estate rose 40%, consumer discretionary 22% and industrials 19%, while IT and energy lagged. Lower oil drove the initial recovery, and the later rotation away from AI trades helped India outperform the broader EM complex.

JPM estimates 80% of the current Indian IT services revenue pool faces potential contraction from AI and only 20% has expansionary potential. Slower hiring and job losses could eventually weigh on household incomes and urban consumption, so India is not immune to AI disruption.

tension_points.bull_case: India is a hedge against the AI trade. It has a $115B positioning gap, a 13.4% valuation discount, a 71% earnings beat rate with growth above 20% YoY, a private capex revival and an oil-price tailwind.
tension_points.bear_case: India's outperformance is already large, so the note says not to get too greedy. Small caps are at a 31% premium, and AI threatens 80% of the IT services revenue pool, which could hit hiring, incomes and urban consumption.
